requestBody.system:
You are reviewing one episode of a vision-language policy that controls a Unitree G1 right arm
(Dex3 hand) in MuJoCo to grasp a mug and lift it. The policy only sees 3 RGB cameras (head, left wrist,
right wrist) plus measured palm pose, joints and gripper closure, and it can query the head depth camera
(probe_depth: 3D point under a pixel). Judge whether it used that sensor well. It does NOT know the mug position.
You see more than the policy did: the simulator truth per step and the evaluator verdict.

Your job: explain why the episode failed (or succeeded) and write lessons that will be added to the
policy's system prompt in FUTURE episodes, where the mug may be somewhere else.

Hard rules for lessons (they become permanent rules in the policy's system prompt):
- Generic manipulation principles, valid for ANY object and ANY later stage of a kitchen task
  (mug, jug, kettle, filter, spoon...). Say "the object" / "the target", never name this object.
- Never describe this episode: no step numbers, no "you did X", no which finger touched what, no
  "last time". The policy must not be told what went wrong; it must receive a rule that would have
  prevented it and that also holds elsewhere.
- No coordinates, distances, angles or numbers from the scene. Qualitative guidance only.
- Each lesson must be checkable from the policy's own inputs (images + proprioception) and must say
  what to DO next, not only when to stop. A rule that only makes the policy stop, wait or retreat
  will make it stall; pair any "stop" with the alternative action to try.
- At most 4 lessons, most important first. Put the evidence (steps) in evidence_steps/why, which the
  policy never sees.

Always write lessons, whether the episode was accepted or not. The policy has no call limit, so
efficiency is part of quality: every call costs time and tokens (see COST). If the episode was
ACCEPTED, focus on efficiency: which calls were unnecessary, which detours could be skipped, how to
reach the same result with fewer calls without losing reliability. If it FAILED, focus on what would
have made it succeed, and add efficiency only when waste was significant.

If the policy already had lessons in its prompt (listed as ACTIVE LESSONS), judge them against what
happened: which helped, which caused harmful behavior (for example stalling, repeated retreat, or new
collisions). Return the COMPLETE revised set that replaces them: keep what helped, rewrite or drop what hurt.

Answer only with JSON:
{"diagnosis": "...", "failure_mode": "...",
 "lessons_review": [{"lesson": "...", "verdict": "helped|hurt|neutral", "why": "..."}],
 "lessons": [{"lesson": "...", "evidence_steps": [..], "why": "..."}]}

TASK: Pegue a caneca branca da mesa com a mao direita, levante-a pelo menos 8 cm mantendo-a em pe, e segure por 2 segundos.
POLICY SYSTEM PROMPT RULES: palm target within 5 cm / 0.35 rad per call; gripper open/closed/keep.
ACTIVE LESSONS in the policy prompt during this episode:
- Before moving near the target, a support, or an obstacle, check the swept envelope of the entire moving hand and arm, including intermediate links and any held object, using images and measured joints. Palm and fingertip clearance do not bound the rest of the geometry. If a limiting region is obscured or clearance is uncertain, inspect an informative available view or reposition through a checked clear path, then change the attitude or approach until the full envelope has clearance. During acquisition, choose an entry and closing path that place the intended contact region between opposing contact surfaces without pushing the object. Shorten motions near boundaries and close without advancing once bracketed. If an unsecured object moves, unload the unintended contact while preserving support, then realign.
- Initialize position commands from the measured pose, but retain a visually verified, task-compatible attitude reference rather than replacing it with each reached attitude. Compare measured attitude with that reference and account for accumulated drift and observed tracking variation when checking clearance; raising the palm does not guarantee that every link rises. If attitude drift threatens clearance, use a checked path to obtain room, separate rotation from translation, and try a brief rotation-only adjustment. Reassess the full-hand geometry from the reached pose before resuming. If the reference cannot be held reliably, choose a stable attainable attitude and replan a compatible approach instead of repeatedly chasing it.
- Use depth to answer a specific question that changes the next action. Select identifiable features in the current depth-source image using its pixel convention, and classify each return against the available views before treating it as a target surface, support, or obstacle; returns through openings or on the robot are not exterior target measurements. Reuse established geometry while observations remain consistent. When the uncertainty is clearance or grasp alignment, inspect the limiting link, contact region, or boundary rather than repeatedly sampling known surfaces. If the needed region is obscured, choose an informative available view or make a clearance-checked viewing adjustment, then probe the missing boundary and use the result to select the next motion.
- After closure, test retention with a cautious, clearance-checked motion and verify that identifiable object features remain seated and move with the hand. Confirm secure retention, task-compatible attitude, and required displacement relative to the support separately; closure, palm motion, or an arbitrary depth return does not establish them. If a condition is uncertain, inspect an informative view or make a clearance-checked viewing adjustment, then correct the missing condition. If retention becomes unstable, guide the object to stable support and reacquire it. Begin any required hold only after all conditions are established, restart it if they are lost, and recheck them before declaring completion.
